blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: Is hydro jetting safe for my sewer line?
items.preview: If the pipe is intact, yes. We check first.
items.answer: If the pipe is sound, yes. We camera it first. If a section is broken or collapsed, a [repair](/mokena/sewer-repair) comes first.

items.q: Will jetting fix a sag in my line?
items.preview: It cleans it out, but it can't lift the pipe.
items.answer: No. Jetting flushes the sludge out of a low spot, which helps, but the sag will collect debris again. A spot repair fixes the slope.

items.q: How is hydro jetting different from rodding?
items.preview: Rodding opens a path. Jetting cleans the whole pipe.
items.answer: Rodding cuts through a clog. Jetting scours the entire pipe wall, removing grease, scale and roots instead of punching a hole through them.

items.q: How long do the results last?
items.preview: Often years for grease. Roots grow back over time.
items.answer: For grease and sludge, often several years with good habits. Roots will eventually return if the joint they came through is still open.

items.answer: It depends on the length of the line, access and how much buildup there is. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
